title: Add representative workload runners and reporting pipeline v7 (benchmark-lab)
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: stabilize and standardize representative workload runners used by the benchmark lab, add a robust reporting pipeline that produces daily aggregates and dashboard-ready artifacts, and introduce profiling baselines for common model classes. This PR is the v7 iteration after field testing v4-v6; it focuses on reliability, parameterization, and CI automation. What changed: 1) Added a new representative runner harness (benchmark-lab/runners/representative_runner.py) that supports pluggable workload profiles (conversational, instruction, embedding-only) and parameterized sequence-length distributions; 2) Implemented a lightweight caching layer in the runner to reuse KV prefixes across similar requests which reduces redundant model KV recomputation; 3) Added profiling baseline definitions and README under benchmark-lab/profiling/baselines to capture target p95/p50, memory, and KV cache hit-rate for each model class; 4) Implemented a reporting pipeline (benchmark-lab/reporting/pipeline_v2.py) that ingests raw run outputs, computes daily aggregates (latency percentiles, token-cost, throughput), writes JSON summaries to S3, and publishes metadata to the benchmark database; 5) Added CI automation and a scheduled workflow ci/workflows/benchmark-report.yml that runs representative smoke workloads on merge to main and uploads artifacts to the test S3 bucket; 6) Updated configs and docs (redwood-configs/benchmarks.yaml, docs/benchmark-lab.md) and added end-to-end tests for the harness. Key results from internal runs: representative conversational workload shows a 12% improvement in median latency and a 9% reduction in p95 when the caching layer is enabled under steady load; throughput improved by ~8% for batched runs on A100; baseline profiles added for llama-family and mixtral-family. Rollout plan: merge to main, enable scheduled workflow in staging for 24 hours, monitor dashboard and roll-forward to production if no regressions observed. Checklist: [x] runner harness implemented, [x] caching layer implemented and covered by unit tests, [x] reporting pipeline implemented, [x] CI workflow added and green on rerun, [x] docs and usage examples added, [x] performance smoke tests added and passed. Related tickets: ENG-3251, ENG-3348. Notes: the reporting pipeline currently writes to the test S3 bucket by default; production bucket will be configured by infra after an ops review. No breaking changes to the serving runtime API are introduced by this PR.

Author reply: included metadata, added model_name, quantization, kernel_hint, and runner_profile fields to the daily summary format.
Samir Gupta: suggest running the harness on a scaled-down Dedicated cluster to validate autoscaling behavior; also confirm that credentials for S3 uploads are scoped to the test bucket only.

release_notes: Add representative workload runners and a production-ready reporting pipeline for the benchmark lab. Includes KV caching for reduced latency, profiling baselines for common model classes, and CI automation to produce daily aggregates uploaded to S3. Improves median latency by ~12% in internal smoke runs and adds new baseline artifacts for dashboards.
